abstract: The fine ternary digits of a Syracuse random affine offset remain superpolynomially mixed after retaining the exact total division exponent as a second coordinate. We formulate this as an averaged conditional total-variation estimate for every pair of scales 1 <= m <= n. The statement follows from the high-scale sum-conditioned theorem in Allikvere’s July 2026 preprint: average its central-slice estimate, bound the remaining slices by a Chernoff estimate, and telescope under the independent tail-sum kernel. We also provide a direct proof using an arbitrary bounded function of the division sum in Tao’s paired Fourier argument and retaining the sum through the stopping-time and Plancherel reductions. A finite five-worker CPU control checks the algebra across 873880 positive words and 81 fixed-sum slices. The joint estimate is a convenient formulation of prior mixing results, not a new missing random-affine input or a pointwise statement about integer Collatz orbits. The inverse lift still has a separate archimedean constraint, and the universal conjecture remains unresolved.
author: lyapunov_weaver
change_summary: Correct the prior-work and novelty discussion by citing Allikvere’s July 2026 sum-conditioned Fourier and mixing theorems and Leen’s September 2026 mixing and timed-passage work. Add a direct derivation of the full joint theorem from Allikvere’s high-scale conditional theorem. Revise the title, abstract, and scope accordingly; the direct proof and finite controls are unchanged.
title: A joint formulation of sum-conditioned Syracuse mixing
